text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mostly higher as the market rebounded from this week's sharp fall on fund-led long liquidation. August added $2.30 to close at $319.90 per tonne. October closed $1.80 higher at $316.0 per tonne.

In New York raw sugar futures settled higher across the board despite a weakening of the July/October spread. July added 7 points to close at 11.15 cents/lb, while October closed 11 points higher at 11.26 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 10 and 12 points. Open interest in the July contract fell by 2,183 lots to 28,775 lots. There was no fresh news to influence prices.

POLAND - Sugar beet production in Poland in 1997/98 is estimated at between 12.8 to 13.6 million tonnes, down from 16.75 million tonnes the previous year. This is largely the result of the lower area sown to sugar beet which fell from 451,000 ha in 1996 to 380,000 ha in 1997. Sugar production in 1997/98 could be between 1.7 and 2.0 million tonnes, white value, down from 2.3 million tonnes produced in 1996/97 but up from 1.6 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. Industry sources said that consumption in 1997/98 could be between 1.63 to 1.64 million tonnes which would leave quite a bit of sugar for export. The government decided to subsidize exports of 113,400 tonnes in 1997/98. The minimum sugar wholesale price for 1997/98 has been set at 1.5 zlotys per kg, up from 1.33 zlotys in 1996/97.

UKRAINE - Sovecon Ltd., an independent research organization specializing in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, said that Ukrainian sugar beet production in 1997 could be between 24 to 26 million tonnes, compared with 23 million tonnes in 1996 and the 1991/95 yearly average of 31.3 million tonnes. However, this does not necessarily mean that production will be higher as the sugar sector faces serious problems. This season, the state planned to increase applications of organic fertilizers by 0.7 tonnes per ha and mineral fertilizers by 13.5 kg per ha, to achieve average yields of 22.3 tonnes per ha. A greater planted area was supposed to increase sugar beet output by 25.2 per cent to 28.8 million tonnes but none of these targets will be reached. The area sown to sugar beet for example fell to 1.164 million ha, down from 1.418 million ha the previous year. SOUTH AFRICA - Sugar production in 1997/98 could rise by more than 10 per cent to 2.5 million tonnes, tel quel, up from 2.27 million tonnes in 1996/97, the South African Sugar Millers' Association said. In the 1996/97 season 44 per cent of all sugar produced was exported an early indications are that this will rise to 48 per cent in 1997/98, it was said. Export earnings are expected to reach 1.46 bln rand, an increase of 271 million over the previous season.

CZECH REPUBLIC ** - Sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 7,521 tonnes, raw value, up from 1,275 tonnes exported in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in 1996/97 up 54,022 tonnes compared to 17,202 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 27,684 tonnes compared to 35,029 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in January/April 1997 were Poland with 20,357 tonnes whites and Slovakia with 1,953 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 40,550 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 42.889 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on June 25. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to June 25 reached 2,290,125 tonnes, which compares to 2,487,498 tonnes last year.

According to trade sources Pakistan has resold 2 to 4 cargoes back to the suppliers before arrival. This could mean that the country which has featured as a good buyer in recent months is possibly overbought.
